sections.h2: What are my realistic options for a quick sale in Texas City?
sections.html:
Texas City owners can go through an agent, a cash buyer, or an as-is negotiation, and a house with storm history, deferred repairs or title questions often suits a buyer who does not need a mortgage. The right option depends on your closing date, your payoff and what an inspector would find.

Texas City sits on the southwestern shore of Galveston Bay in Galveston County, and that geography shapes the questions buyers ask. Expect them to ask about water, drainage, insurance and roof age before they ask about paint. Gathering paperwork early speeds up any route.

  • Agent listing: best exposure, with inspections and lender timelines.
  • Cash sale as is: fewer contingencies and a closing date you choose.
  • Delayed closing: workable when you need time to move or settle an estate.

sections.h2: How did a duck-hunting trip turn into Texas City?
sections.html:
The Handbook of Texas says three brothers from Duluth, Minnesota, saw potential for a major port in the marshes of Shoal Point on a hunting trip in 1891, joined other Duluth shippers to buy 10,000 acres of bay frontage, and renamed the place Texas City. The first townsite plat was filed on May 17, 1893, and the city incorporated on September 16, 1911.

Refining arrived after 1908, and the entry credits wartime industry with pushing the city to fourth among Texas ports by 1941. Population went from 16,620 in 1950 to 32,065 in 1960. On April 16, 1947, a ship loaded with ammonium nitrate exploded in the harbor, killing 576 people and injuring more than 4,000. Hurricane Carla in 1961 brought four feet of floodwater over much of the city.

The response was physical. The Handbook describes a barrier seawall begun in 1962 and finished in 1985, an eight-foot inner levee at Moses Lake built in 1982 with pumps, and the end of local groundwater pumping because subsidence was adding to flooding. The city grew fast in the 1940s and 1950s, so check your own deed and permit records for the age of the house and the work done on it.

sections.h2: What draws buyers to Texas City?
sections.html:
Jobs, schools and water draw them. The Handbook describes ten major refining and petrochemical industries forming the base of the port, with growth running west from the bay.

It also lists the Nessler Civic Center, a 55-acre tract holding the city's largest park, the library, city hall and the stadium, plus the Texas City Dike and Moses Lake as recreation areas. Texas City Independent School District dates to July 11, 1905, and College of the Mainland opened in September 1967.

  • Plant and port workers value a short drive to work.
  • Commuters toward Houston or Galveston weigh the 25.7-minute average commute in the Census data.
  • Families look at the school district and the parks.

sections.h2: What do the QuickFacts numbers show for Texas City?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists 59,733 residents in the July 2025 estimate, 15.2 percent above the 2020 base. A growing city draws buyers, which helps a seller who prices in line with nearby sales.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax and appraisal protests in Texas City?
sections.html:
Galveston Central Appraisal District values Texas City property. Its customer service office is at 9850 Emmett F. Lowry Expressway, Suite A101, Texas City, TX 77591, with weekday hours listed as 7:30 to 5:30 Monday through Thursday and Friday mornings until noon, and its phone is (409) 935-1980.

GCAD takes exemption applications by mail, online or at the office and says it acts within 90 days. A protest can be filed through its taxpayer portal, where you register with the owner ID and eFile PIN from your notice, and the online protest counts as your informal hearing. If no agreement is reached, the case goes to the appraisal review board.

  • The board meets in panels of three; hearings typically run 15 to 20 minutes.
  • You can attend by phone or videoconference, by written affidavit, or in person.
  • A final order arrives by certified mail roughly three to four weeks later.
  • One reschedule is allowed for any reason; hearings begin in May each year.

The filing deadline is May 15 or 30 days after your notice, whichever is later, and GCAD says owners who want to appeal the board's decision can choose binding arbitration or district court.

sections.h2: What tax deadlines come into play at a Texas City closing?
sections.html:
The Comptroller says bills go out around October 1 and taxes become delinquent on February 1 if unpaid by January 31, when a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest attach. The lien dates to January 1, so your closing agent settles the year's tax before funding.

Homestead owners who qualify can get a school tax ceiling, and GCAD notes that a person with a disability can qualify under the Social Security definition even without receiving benefits. Ask the Galveston County tax office for a payoff through your closing date.

sections.h2: Can my tax ceiling or exemption move with me?
sections.html:
Possibly. GCAD says that a disabled owner's school tax ceiling can transfer as a percentage to a new qualifying Texas homestead, and that a ceiling for county, city or junior college taxes can move if you stay within the same taxing unit and that unit has adopted one. A surviving spouse who is 55 or older and keeps the home can continue the exemptions.

GCAD's homestead page also lists the exemption types it handles: general residential, disabled person, age 65 or older, 100 percent disabled veteran, a donated residence of a partially disabled veteran, and surviving spouses of veterans or service members killed in action. If you are leaving Texas City for another Texas address, ask GCAD about the request to cancel or port an exemption before you close, so the paperwork is in order.

sections.h2: What storm and condition records should I assemble?
sections.html:
Prepare a clear answer to the questions buyers will raise: whether the house has taken on water, what repairs followed, and what insurance covers.

  • Insurance claim records, repair invoices and any elevation certificate you hold.
  • Photos of the roof, slab, drains and electrical panel.
  • Paperwork for any foundation work.
  • A check with the city permit office on whether past repairs were permitted.

A cash buyer taking the house as is will weigh these items in the price rather than require repairs, but records still help.

sections.h2: What about foreclosure, inheritance or tenants?
sections.html: Texas auctions run on the first Tuesday of a month after 21 days' notice, so a sale beforehand can protect equity. An inherited house needs someone with authority to sign, and a tenant is owed written notice to vacate before any court case. After a notary acknowledges your signature, the deed is filed with the Galveston County Clerk.

faqs.q: Must I repair storm damage before selling in Texas City?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer can take the house as is and price repairs. Disclose what you know and keep invoices, since buyers ask.

faqs.q: Which office handles my Texas City appraisal?
faqs.a: Galveston Central Appraisal District at (409) 935-1980, or visit its Texas City office. The protest window runs to May 15 or 30 days after the notice, whichever is later.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax on a Texas City sale?
faqs.a: Ask your title company. The county clerk pages describe recording fees, so your closing statement is where charges show up.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Texas City house I inherited?
faqs.a: Often yes, once someone has authority to sign. Confirm which paperwork you need with a Texas probate attorney.

faqs.q: How soon can a Texas City sale close?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close as fast as the title work allows, often within a few weeks, while a financed sale depends on the lender. Liens and back taxes can slow either path.
